claims.text: The starting material is an as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloy.
The starting samples are produced by arc-melting or melt-spinning.
The as-deposited alloy has an ordered, single-phase hexagonal structure.
The as-deposited alloy undergoes a sharp, first-order magnetostructural transition with substantial hysteresis.
The baseline material has limited heat-exchange performance because of its low surface-to-volume ratio.
Rapid thermal annealing below the recrystallization threshold can refine the grains without changing the primary phase.
Annealing at approximately 0.8 times the phase melting temperature for seconds to minutes in an inert atmosphere is an appropriate treatment window.
Rapid thermal annealing produces a high density of nanostructured grain boundaries.
The induced grain boundaries act as heterogeneous nucleation sites for the magnetostructural transition.
A higher grain-boundary density lowers local interfacial strain-energy barriers to transformation.
Lower transformation barriers produce a more spatially distributed and gradual magnetostructural transformation.
A more gradual transformation broadens the temperature window of the magnetocaloric response.
Reducing interfacial strain barriers reduces magnetocaloric hysteresis and associated losses.
Annealed samples will have a slightly lower peak magnetic entropy change than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples will exhibit a broader and more gradual magnetocaloric transition than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples will exhibit significantly lower hysteresis losses under low-field magnetic cycling.
The refined microstructure will improve effective heat exchange during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
The predictions apply near the transition temperature only while the primary hexagonal phase is retained and unwanted secondary phases are avoided.
Conditions that cause substantial grain growth or phase decomposition are outside the proposed valid regime.

contradictions.description: The material is repeatedly labeled 'as-deposited' and the treatment 'post-deposition,' but arc-melted ingots are included as an initial and baseline state without identifying any deposition step. This makes the sample-state definition internally inconsistent.

The treatment is required to remain below the recrystallization threshold while also being specified as approximately 0.8×Tm, but no recrystallization threshold is given to establish that these two requirements are compatible.
